text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today despite a week and a half of strong gains, as oil prices ticked down in a volatile environment. Crude oil prices remain elevated—US oil at $107.89 and global Brent at $115.22—but traders appear to be taking a breath after several days of geopolitical fear-buying. The stock's small decline reflects this momentary pause rather than a fundamental shift; the underlying support from Middle East tensions (Iranian strike threats, Saudi disruptions, Houthi attacks on oil infrastructure) remains in place.

The bigger picture is that energy prices have stayed well above $100 per barrel precisely because of these regional risks, which has kept the stock up 8% over two weeks. Any sustained pullback in crude would be the real test of whether this rally holds, but for now the geopolitical floor supporting oil—and integrated majors like ConocoPhillips—looks intact.
